items.title: Add hang-stemware-rack: Hang washed wine glasses upside down in an overhead bar rack
items.body:
Adds `tasks/hang-stemware-rack/` (task.json, README.md, task.py, robocurve_ext.py, glass.obj, test_task.py).

A bartender's closing step: washed stemmed glasses come out of the glass washer bowl-down and go straight into the
overhead rack the same way, so they drain and stay clear of dust. The rack is a channel with two lips; each glass's
stem goes up into the gap between the lips at the open end and its foot is slid along the lips until the glass hangs.
Single-channel bar racks have a 25 mm channel, an 89 mm opening and a 38 mm profile and take bases up to 76-83 mm
(KegWorks brass glass hanger rack; WebstaurantStore Regency 460GHRG16 and American Metalcraft GR1435).

Here the rack's lips are 22 cm above the table, with an open end on the robot's right and a closed end 30 cm along.
Two wine glasses (75 mm foot, 9 mm by 80 mm stem, 84 mm bowl, 178 mm tall, 180 g) stand bowl-down on a bar mat. A
glass can only go in through the open end: its foot is wider than the 25 mm channel, so the stem has to enter at the
end and run along the gap with the foot riding just above the lips, before the glass is lowered to hang by its foot.
The only place to hold it is the 9 mm stem, under the overhead rack, so the hand comes in nearly level and grips the
stem low enough that the foot clears the lips while the hand clears their underside.

Score, once everything is still: 1.0 when both glasses hang (foot underside within 3 mm of the lips' top, stem within
8 mm of the channel's centre line, the whole foot inside the rack, tilt at most 5 deg) and both grippers are at least
3 cm from each glass; 0.5 for one glass; 0 otherwise, or if any glass was knocked over (tipped past 45 deg) at any
time during the trial.

The rack and its posts are compound rigid bodies of box pieces, and each glass is three convex parts from `glass.obj`,
built by `robocurve_ext.py` shipped in the task folder; nothing in `yam_arena` on disk changes. No third-party assets.

Runs (RTX 5090, `object_jitter=0`, default seed): scripted demo 1.0, success at step 640 (the last frame shows both glasses hanging bowl-down under the rack and the mat empty; each foot on the lips, tilt 0.0 deg); Dream-1 0.0 over the full 900-step run limit (the right arm nudged glass A about 7 mm, and it settled back upright, but neither glass was lifted). Offline tests: 22 passed.

items.title: Add task: Wrap a pipe thread with thread-seal tape from a dispenser, the way the fitting turns on
items.body:
Adds `tasks/wrap-a-pipe-thread-with-thread-seal-tape-from-a-dispenser-the-way-the-fitting-turns-on/`.

A 3/4-inch pipe nipple stands upright in a floor flange, its male thread at the top, and a handheld PTFE tape dispenser lies on a mat beside it. The robot must wrap the thread, ready for a fitting to be screwed on, and put the dispenser back. The instruction does not state the trade standard that is scored: wound the way the fitting turns on (clockwise seen from the thread's end; wound the other way the tape bunches and the joint leaks), 3 to 6 turns covering the thread with the first thread left bare, torn off and its tail pressed down. PhysX has no tape, so it is our own model: the tape is wound by the roll's path round the pipe, comes off only as the roll turns on the dispenser's braked spindle (a PhysX hinge), and its stretch pulls the roll round; a steady wrap pays out at 0.2 to 0.6 N, and a yank outruns the braked roll and tears the tape at 1.5 N.

- Scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (success at step 609 of 1,600; four turns clockwise, the thread covered, the tail pressed down by the second hand)
- Media: M-4KYK3E
- Shortcut checks (`TAPE_DEMO=backwards`, `TAPE_DEMO=nopress`): the same wrap anticlockwise scores 0; the tail left standing scores 0.5
- Offline checks of the tape model (including that a roll which cannot turn tears the tape in its first turn), every scoring tier, and the demo's reach and per-step limits: `python -m pytest -q test_tape_wrap.py` (33 tests)

items.title: Assemble a 2x2 18650 battery pack in a jig
items.body:
## Assemble a 2x2 18650 battery pack in a jig

* **Task board:** TK-8T7FNK
* **Category:** Impact on jobs
* **Run limit:** 2,400 steps (2 minutes at 20 Hz)

**Task:** With your left gripper, put the black battery holder half that lies cups up into the orange jig. With your right gripper, take the four yellow batteries from the grey tray one at a time and push each into a cup of that holder, positive end up. Then, with your left gripper, pick up the other holder half, which lies cups down, lower it onto the tops of the four batteries, and move both arms back to where they started.

**Description:** Building small lithium-ion packs is everyday work at battery, e-bike and electronics repair benches: the bottom half of a cell holder goes into an assembly jig, the cells are pushed into its cups all the same way round (a reversed cell shorts the pack once it is welded), and the top half of the holder is pressed on to hold them before the nickel strips are welded. The scene starts with an orange assembly jig screwed to the table, two identical halves of a 2x2 18650 holder beside it (one cups up, one cups down) and a grey tray of four cells standing positive end up. The holder's cups leave 0.3 mm around each cell, so each has to come down square over its cup.

**Scores:** Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms reached over the jig, the holder halves and the cell tray again and again, but it never picked up a holder half or a cell); demo: 1.0 (all four steps by step 1892, success at step 1971)

### Setup

![Setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/girardijp3/benchmark-tasks/media/battery-pack-assembly/setup.png)

| Dream-1 run (GIF at 2x speed) | Scripted demo |
|---|---|
| [![Dream-1 run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/girardijp3/benchmark-tasks/media/battery-pack-assembly/dream_top.gif)](https://github.com/girardijp3/benchmark-tasks/blob/media/battery-pack-assembly/dream_top.mp4) | [![Scripted demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/girardijp3/benchmark-tasks/media/battery-pack-assembly/demo_top.gif)](https://github.com/girardijp3/benchmark-tasks/blob/media/battery-pack-assembly/demo_top.mp4) |

### Scoring: four steps, 0.25 each

| Step | Done when |
|---|---|
| 1. Bottom holder in the jig | at the end a holder half lies cups up in the jig's pocket, centred within 2 mm |
| 2. Two cells seated | at the end, with step 1, at least two cells sit in cups (bottom within 1 mm of the cup's axis), + end up within 8° |
| 3. Four cells seated | all four |
| 4. Top holder on | at the end, with step 3, the other half lies turned over on the cells, within 2 mm of the bottom half's axis |

1.0 when all four hold, both arms are back where they started (within 3 cm) holding nothing, and both halves and all cells are still for 1 s. 0 if a holder half, a cell or the tray falls off the table.

Top camera, 20 Hz control, 240 Hz physics. Run commands, scoring and assets: [README](https://github.com/girardijp3/benchmark-tasks/blob/battery-pack-assembly/tasks/battery-pack-assembly/README.md).

items.title: Weigh out 1.00 g of granules on an analytical balance with a draft shield
items.body:
## Weigh out 1.00 g of granules on an analytical balance with a draft shield

- **Category:** Impact on jobs
- **Run limit:** 2,400 steps (2 minutes at 20 Hz)

**Task:** Weigh out 1.00 g of the orange granules into the weighing boat on the analytical balance. Slide the balance's glass top door open by its dark handle, put the empty weighing boat in the middle of the pan and slide the door shut. Press the green TARE key, so the display reads 0.00 with the empty boat on the pan. Open the door again and pour granules from the vial into the boat, a little at a time, until the display reads 1.00 g. Then slide the door shut. Do not spill granules, and do not press TARE again once granules are in the boat.

**Description:** Weighing a set mass of a powder into a tared container, with the draft shield shut for the zero and the reading, is a daily step in sample and solution preparation. Pouring too fast overshoots, and an untared container or an open door gives a wrong mass.

**How it differs from other weighing tasks:** the robot doses loose granules from a vial to a target reading within ±0.01 g, watching the balance display as it pours, instead of placing whole weights or parts on a scale; and the draft shield must be slid shut for the tare and for the final reading, in that order.

**Scores:** Dream-1 run: 0.0 (it reached over the balance but never opened the door or moved the boat), demo: 1.0 (one hand slid the top door open, shut and opened it again and pressed TARE with the empty boat on the pan; the other hand placed the boat and poured from the vial until the display read 1.00 g, with the door shut at the end and nothing spilled)

### Setup

![Setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jingyi-Z/benchmark-tasks/media/analytical-balance/setup.png)

| Dream-1 run | Scripted demo |
|---|---|
| [![Dream-1 run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jingyi-Z/benchmark-tasks/media/analytical-balance/dream_top.gif)](https://github.com/Jingyi-Z/benchmark-tasks/blob/media/analytical-balance/dream_top.mp4) | [![Scripted demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jingyi-Z/benchmark-tasks/media/analytical-balance/demo_top.gif)](https://github.com/Jingyi-Z/benchmark-tasks/blob/media/analytical-balance/demo_top.mp4) |

items.body:
Adds `tasks/file-a-steel-block-flat-down-to-a-scribed-line/`.

A mild steel bar is clamped in a machinist's vise with its top 1 mm above a scribed line. The robot must file the top down to the line, keeping it flat, and put the file back on its rest: the first exercise of every fitting and machining apprenticeship. The file cuts only on the push, both hands must press evenly or it rocks and rounds the work, and filed below the line the part is spoilt (latched 0). PhysX cannot cut, so the cut is our own model: the file stands on springs we compute and each section of the top is lowered in proportion to pressure times distance slid on push strokes.

- Scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (success at step 801 of 1,600; the top ends 0.08 to 0.12 mm above the line, flat within 0.04 mm)

items.title: Add detent-latch bottle opening task
items.body:
Open a free-standing bottle by lowering its detented safety loop and pressing a separate rocker to release the spring-opening lid. The task uses the official YAM station, contact-constrained passive mechanism geometry, numeric partial credit, and evaluator-only wrist reaction measurements.

Recorded results: Dream-1 beta 0.0 over 2400 steps/120 s with 592 requests in one continuous server session and no expired retries; scripted contact demo 1.0 in 405 steps/20.25 s. Model/demo videos and setup screenshot are uploaded as media M-ANXZMU. The task folder includes its evaluation runner, continuity gate and offline scorer.

Validation: 24 tests pass; an isolated copy of the task reproduces the offline results. A 320-step negative contact probe presses the rocker to 12.7 degrees with the safety loop raised while the lid stays closed. A table-support scoring gap was corrected after recording; all 405 demo and 2400 model measurements satisfy the added criterion, preserving scores and credit times. A 20-step live simulation checks the new evaluator/measurement path. Geometry, physics and controller behavior were unchanged.

The board review compared the nearby push-and-turn medicine bottle, alternative-opening pouring bottle and simultaneous dual-latch case. This task instead requires the sequential hinged safety loop and separate rocker on a free bottle. Dynamics are approximate; no randomized success-rate sweep or hardware validation is claimed. See the task README and yam/submission-audit.json for reproduction and limits.

items.title: Add elastic headphones task
items.body:
Adds a dual-arm task that prepares folded headphones for use at a shared listening station: pull the inward-folded earcup out from inside the headband, turn both earcups to their wearing positions, and hang the headband in a U-shaped cradle. The headset has a passive elastic headband and folding/swivel joints; the stand is a free rigid body.

Final-state credit is 0.4 for unfolding (both folding joints within 15 degrees of fully unfolded), 0.2 for each earcup turned to its wearing position within 15 degrees, and 0.2 for stable hanging after releasing both hands for five seconds. The package includes self-contained USDs, the calibrated YAM scene, evaluation and scoring code, and recorded-state video rendering.

## Evaluation

- **Dream-1 beta:** 0.0/1.0 in 120 seconds, using camera images and measured robot joint/gripper positions at 20 Hz.
- **Demo policy:** 1.0/1.0 in 79.833 seconds, using a fixed open-loop action script at 30 Hz. The policy uses no privileged simulator information or observation feedback during execution; independent scoring and recording measurements do not feed back into control.

Both evaluations use seed 0, the same fixed layout and native YAM actuator settings. The full demo passes all scoring components, with zero robot contact during the final five seconds. Scene, camera, action and scoring checks passed; saved states reproduce the reported scores.

items.body:
## Feed filament into the feeder on top of a 3D printer

* **Task board:** TK-VUHB93
* **Category:** Impact on jobs
* **Run limit:** 1,200 steps (1 minute at 20 Hz)

**Task:** Feed the free end of the orange filament into the brass inlet of the black feeder on top of the printer, at its back right, until at least 2 cm of it is inside, then let go.

**Description:** Loading an enclosed 3D printer by hand: the filament comes off the spool on the printer's side holder and its cut end is pushed into the feeder on the roof, a funnel narrowing to a bore barely wider than the filament. items.title: Add task: Fit a blanking panel at U6 of a server rack
items.body:
Adds `tasks/rack-blanking-panel/` (Impact on AI timelines). This replaces #902, which was withdrawn to fix the scorer's release check.

The instruction is "Fit the blanking panel at U6."

The scene:
- A 19-inch two-post 8U rack stands on the table.
- A server, a switch and a patch panel are installed, and U4 to U7 are empty.
- A 1U blanking panel stands in a slotted stand in front of the rack.

The robot has to:
- find U6 on the posts (units are counted from the bottom, three square holes per unit);
- carry the 48 cm panel to the rack;
- put the clips at its two ends into U6's middle holes;
- push both ends home and let go.

Scoring:
- 1.0: fitted at U6 with both ends home and the robot clear for 1 s.
- 0.5: fitted at U6 but still held, or only one end home.
- 0: another unit, or one hole off (the panel straddling two units).

Results:
- Media: M-XRFNCY (Dream-1 run, demo, setup screenshot). Both videos show all three cameras: top, left arm and right arm.
- Scores: Dream-1 run 0.0; scripted demo 1.0 (288 steps).
- Scripted variants that fit the panel one hole too high (straddling U6 and U7) or at U5 score 0. One that fits it at U6 but never lets go scores 0.5.

Changed since #902:
- "Let go" now measures yam_arena's collision hulls of every link, the gripper body and both fingers, at their simulated poses. It used to measure capsules, and those missed an open hand resting on the panel.

Run and demo commands, scoring details, the real-world build and simulation fidelity are in the task's README.md.

items.title: Snap a circuit board out of its panel over the break edge
items.body:
This task tests controlled depaneling. The robot slides a scored panel until its V-score sits on a break block's edge, holds the frame down with one arm and bends the populated board downward with the other until it snaps off. It then puts the board in an ESD tray and leaves the scrap frame on the block or flat on the bench. The scorer checks the separation direction from pose history: a break made off the edge, by twisting, by lifting or by pulling scores zero. Hand-breaking scored panels over an edge is routine in small-batch electronics assembly, and it needs registration, a bimanual brace-and-bend and careful transfer of a part that has just been freed.

- `task.json`: instruction, context, full setup, scoring tiers, run limit, reset and fidelity notes
- `README.md`: run and score commands, a rebuild-from-text setup, scoring rules with their rationale, and the demo and physics parameters
- `snap_board_out_of_panel.py`: scene (break block, frame, board, landing nest, ESD tray, passive breakable V-score joint), scorer and scripted demo
